text:
### Observed differences

- Participation itself did not change: A26, A27, A35, A36 and A41 still occur together in every single trace in both windows (co-occurrence 100% in all six pairwise checks), so the differences below concern execution order, not whether activities run. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- The order between the trio A35/A36/A41 and A27 reversed: in the earlier window A27 came before A35, A36 and A41 in about 98–99 in 100 traces; in the later window each of the trio came before A27 in about 97 in 100 traces. [REL004, REL005, REL006]
- The order between the trio and A26 reversed as well: earlier, A26 preceded A35, A36 and A41 in about 98 in 100 traces; later, the trio preceded A26 in about 97–98 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL003]
- A25's hand-over changed: earlier, about 97.5 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions went to A27, which followed A25 immediately (distance 1 in about 98.5 in 100 traces); in the later window its transitions split almost equally among A36 (about 31%), A41 (about 33%) and A35 (about 32%), and A27 followed only four to five positions later (about 90 in 100 at distance 4, about 10 at distance 5). [DIR001, LAG001]
- A26 and A30 became adjacent while the trio lost its link to A30: earlier, A26 led into the trio (A41 about 38%, A35 about 33%, A36 about 28% of its outgoing transitions) and reached A30 four to five positions later (about 93 in 100 at distance 4), with each trio activity reaching A30 within one to three steps; later, A26 led almost exclusively to A30 (about 97.5 in 100 transitions, distance 1 in about 98.5 in 100 traces), and a trio-to-A30 step is practically unobserved (each of the three relations falls from about 200 observations to about 1). [DIR002, LAG003, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
- The trio's exits shifted from A30 to A27: earlier, A35, A36 and A41 each led to the other two and to A30 (roughly 28–38% per successor); later, each still leads to the other two but now to A27 (roughly 27–37%) instead of A30 (under 1%). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two segments between A25 and A30 exchanged their execution order. In the earlier window the sequence ran A25 → A27 → A26 → A35/A36/A41 in varying internal order → A30; in the later window it runs A25 → A35/A36/A41 → A27 → A26 → A30 — the trio A35, A36 and A41 moved from after A27 and A26 to directly after A25, and A30 moved from after the trio to immediately after A26. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003]

The support is direct and consistent: six order reversals each rest on all 200 traces per window, the successor profiles of A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41 all change coherently, the distance shifts match the reversal (A25→A27 from 1 to 4–5 steps; A26→A30 from 4–5 steps to 1), and 21 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.6 expected if nothing had changed is far beyond what an unchanged process produces; constant 100% co-occurrence rules out activities being added, removed or becoming optional. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG003]

Limitations: the relative order of A27 and A26 is not covered by any pairwise item, so their sequence inside the moved segment is inferred from the distance profiles rather than observed directly; and with two 200-trace samples, a flip in the mix of two pre-existing variants cannot be distinguished from a reordering within one behaviour. The distances are event positions, so the change is established for execution order, not for clock timing. [LAG001, LAG003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

Other differences: only minor noise — a handful of rare successors (about 0.5–1% of transitions each) appear or disappear at A25, A35, A36 and A41, and the share of interleaved or repeated executions of the affected pairs stays around 1–3 in 100 in both windows; neither forms a separate behavioural change. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL004]
